Condition : 1 - The development hereby permitted shall be begun before the expiration of three years from the date of this permission.
Reason: To accord with the provisions of Section 92(1) of the Town and Country Planning Act 1990.

Condition : 3 - No development above ground level shall take place until full details and samples of all materials to be used in the construction of the external surfaces of the development hereby permitted have been submitted to and approved in writing by the local planning authority. Details must include a detailed schedule of materials, a photographic sample board and rendered drawings, elevations and sections at a sufficient scale (1:20 or 1:50) to illustrate how all external materials will appear together. The submitted information should cover the following elements:
(a)	Brick/stonework (including brick, stone, masonry, brick panels, feature brick panel, brick framing feature and mortar on-site sample panel, minimum one metre by one metre) including all mortar colours, joint type, brick bond;
(b)	Any cladding materials / render (including specifications);
(c)	Tiles / roof covering; including parapet coping / capping materials, dormers and canopies;
(d)	Window types; and sectional drawings of reveals / courses / sills / textures / head details 
(e)	Balustrading treatment for proposed ramped access (including details / sections / materials); 
(f)	Any boundary treatment (including gates) that may be required; and 
(g)	Any other materials/details / fittings to be used (including solar panels, heat pumps, extract vents, rainwater goods, boiler flues etc.), with sections and on-site samples where appropriate.
The development shall then be carried out in accordance with the approved details and maintained as such thereafter.
Reason: In order to protect the setting of the listed building and the appearance of the conservation area.
Condition : 4 - The development hereby approved insofar as it relates to repairs and infill of the main house shall, as far as practically possible, be carried out with the re-use of the original bricks (both whole and part bricks), in accordance with the approved method statement. No alternatives shall be used until approval has been given in writing by the local planning authority of a sample panel of 0.5m2 utilising the new brick.
The use of any new brick shall be carried out in accordance with the approved details.
Reason: In order to safeguard the special architectural and historic interest of the listed building.
Condition : 5 - The timber treads and mouldings and the outer stringer skirting shall, where possible, be salvaged and reinstated on the new stair frame.  
Reason: In order to safeguard the special architectural and historic interest of the listed building.
Condition : 6 - No external utility boxes (for gas and electricity) shall be affixed to the building and any cables, wires, aerials, pipework, meter boxes or flues shall be discreetly integrated into the building and shall not be fixed to any elevation or roof slope facing a highway. 
No fans, louvres, ducts, water tanks or other external plant shall be installed on the building hereby permitted without the prior written approval of the local planning authority. 
No advertisements shall be displayed on the development without details of the advertisements having first been submitted to and approved in writing by the Council through securing of Advertisement Consent and/or Planning Permission. 
Reason: In order to safeguard the visual amenity of the area and neighbours living conditions.

Condition : 8 - No development shall take place, including any works of demolition, until evidence of the further ecological investigations specified in the submitted Preliminary Ecological Appraisal (dated May 2026) and Preliminary Roost Assessment (dated May 2026) has been submitted to the local planning authority and approved in writing. Any subsequent recommendations following these surveys shall then be adopted prior to, and for the duration of, development works, and any permanent habitat protection or enhancement measures for bats, mammals or other site habitats put in place prior to occupation of the development and retained and managed 
The mitigation measures shall include:
- Obtaining any relevant licences from Natural England (or registration with relevant licensing scheme) to allow proposed works, and therefore destruction of roost/disturbance of any bats, to be undertaken;
- A method statement and commitment for works to be undertaken in accordance;
- Supervised (by a CIEEM certified ecologist) removal of any roosting features with bats found during demolition safely transferred to alternative roosting locations such as bat boxes;
- Provision of alternative roosting features for any identified bats within the proposed scheme, including number and details of exact location, specification and design of the habitats;
- Measures to prevent disturbance to any roosts during construction, habitat enhancements, specifications for lighting, etc.
Reason: To ensure that the development provides the maximum possible provision towards creation of habitats and valuable areas for biodiversity, and to protect the conservation status of bats in particular.
Supporting notes:
Standing Advice from Natural England on bats:
o	Bat surveys and mitigation for development projects - https://www.gov.uk/guidance/bats- surveys-and-mitigation-for-development- projects
o	Bats: protection and licences - https://www.gov.uk/guidance/bats-protection- surveys-and-licences

Condition : 9 - The development shall be carried out in accordance with the recommendations with the approved Arboricultural Impact Assessment & Method Statement (05552R, dated May 2026). The erection of fencing for the protection of all retained trees, hedge or vegetation shall be carried out in complete accordance with BS5837:2012, before any equipment, machinery, or materials are brought onto the site for the purposes of development or other operations. The fencing shall be retained intact for the full duration of the development until all equipment, materials and surplus materials have been removed from the site. If the fencing is damaged all operations shall cease until it is repaired in accordance with the approved details. Nothing shall be stored or placed in any fenced area in accordance with this condition and the ground levels within those areas shall not be altered, nor shall any excavations be made without the written approval of the local planning authority.
Reason: To ensure trees on site are retained.
Condition : 10 - Prior to the first commencement of the hereby approved development, a Biodiversity Gain Plan shall have been submitted to and approved in writing by the local planning authority. The Plan shall include:
(i)	information about the steps taken or to be taken to minimise the adverse effect of the development on the biodiversity of the onsite habitat and any other habitat;
(ii)	the pre-development biodiversity value of the onsite habitat;
(iii)	the post-development biodiversity value of the onsite habitat;
(iv)	any registered offsite biodiversity gain allocated to the development and the biodiversity value of that gain in relation to the development;
(v)	any biodiversity credits purchased for the development; and
(vi)	such other matters as the Secretary of State may by regulations specify;
(vi)	confirmation that a formal agreement has been reached to provide a cash payment towards biodiversity net gain monitoring in line with the Council's adopted fee schedule.
The development shall thereafter be carried out in accordance with the approved Plan, with the monitoring fee having been paid in full, prior to the first occupation of the development. Any habitats created or enhanced on-site and off-site in accordance with the Biodiversity Gain Plan must be maintained thereafter for a minimum of 30 years.
Reason: In the interests of improving Biodiversity and in accordance with The Town and Country Planning Act 1990, Section 90A, Schedule 7A.
Condition : 11 - A) Prior to the first commencement of the hereby approved development a Habitat Management and Monitoring Plan (HMMP) prepared in accordance with the approved Biodiversity Gain Plan shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the local planning authority. The Plan shall include:
(i)	a non-technical summary;
(ii)	the roles and responsibilities of the people or organisation(s) delivering the HMMP
(iii)	the planned habitat creation and enhancement works to create or improve habitat to achieve the biodiversity net gain in accordance with the approved Biodiversity Gain Plan;
(iv)	the management measures to maintain habitat in accordance with the approved Biodiversity Gain Plan for a period of 30 years from the completion of development; and
(v)	the monitoring methodology and frequency in respect of the created or enhanced habitat to be submitted to the local planning authority. 
B) No occupation or use of the hereby approved development shall take place until:
(i)	the habitat creation and enhancement works set out in the approved HMMP have been completed; and
(ii)	a completion report, evidencing the completed habitat enhancements, has been submitted to, and approved in writing by the local planning authority. 
The created and/or enhanced habitat specified in the approved HMMP shall be managed and maintained in accordance with the approved HMMP.
C) Monitoring reports shall be submitted to the local planning authority in writing in accordance with the methodology and frequency specified in the approved HMMP.
Reason: In the interests of improving Biodiversity and in accordance with The Town and Country Planning Act 1990, Section 90A, Schedule 7A.
Condition : 12 - Prior to first occupation of the development, details (e.g. photographs and copies of installation contracts) shall be submitted to the local planning authority for approval in writing, to demonstrate that the development has been carried out in accordance with the following sustainable sourcing of materials requirements:
-	At least three of the key elements of the building envelope (external walls, windows roof, upper floor slabs, internal walls, floor finishes/coverings) are to achieve a rating of A+ to D in the Building Research Establishment (BRE) The Green Guide of specification. 
- 	At least 50% of timber and timber products are to be sourced from accredited Forest Stewardship Council (FSC) or Programme for the Endorsement of Forestry Certification (PEFC) scheme. 
- 	No construction or insulation materials are to be used which would release toxins into the internal and external environment, including those that deplete stratospheric ozone. 
Reason: In order to ensure the sustainable sourcing of materials.
Condition : 13 - a)	The development hereby permitted shall be implemented in accordance with the hereby approved Energy and Sustainability Statement (Issue 1.0, dated April 2026). 
b)	Prior to first occupation of the development, evidence (e.g. photographs, installation contracts and As-Built certificates under the Standard Assessment Procedure/National Calculation Method) shall have been submitted to and approved in writing by the local planning authority to show that these areas of development have been constructed in accordance with the approved Energy Statement to achieve a site-wide carbon reduction in emissions of at least 85% on Part L Building Regulations. 
Reason: To ensure that the development makes the fullest contribution to minimising carbon dioxide emissions.
Condition : 14 - Prior to commencement of development the applicant shall have entered into a formal agreement with the Council to provide the payment specified in the approved Energy and Sustainability Statement (Issue 1.0, dated April 2026) towards its Carbon Offset Fund.
Reason: To ensure the development meets sustainability standards. 
Condition : 15 - Prior to first occupation of the development, full details of the proposed heat pumps shall have been submitted to and approved in writing by the local planning authority. These shall include:
-	An estimate of the heating and/or cooling energy (MWh/annum) the heat pumps would provide to the development and the percentage of contribution to the site's heat loads to demonstrate how the heat fraction from heat pump technologies has been maximised.
-	Details of the Seasonal Coefficient of Performance (SCOP) and/or Seasonal Energy Efficiency ratio (SEER) and how these have been calculated including the expected heat source and heat distribution temperatures (for space heat and hot water) and the distribution loss factor, which shall be calculated based on the above information.
-	Details of all screening and acoustic insulation to protect against visual harm and undue noise and disturbance to surrounding sensitive receptors. 
Development shall be carried out in accordance with the approved details. 
Reason: To achieve appropriate sustainability standards, to protect residents living conditions and to preserve the amenities of the area.
Condition : 16 - Prior to commencement of any above-ground works on the development hereby permitted (except any demolition, site clearance, ground investigation and remediation work), details of the specifications regarding power, number, appearance, location, orientation, total area and predicted carbon savings from the photovoltaic panels shall have been submitted to and approved by the local planning authority to show how the renewable energy carbon savings are to be achieved and maximised. The photovoltaic panels shall be installed in accordance with the approved details prior to the occupation of the relevant part of the development and retained and maintained as such unless otherwise agreed by the local planning authority.
Reason: To achieve appropriate sustainability standards.
Condition : 17 - (a) The cumulative measured or calculated rating level of noise emitted from the air source heat pumps hereby approved shall generate no more than 10dB(A) below the existing background noise level, during all times that the mechanical system is in operation. The measured or calculated noise levels shall be determined at the boundary of the nearest ground floor noise sensitive uses or one metre from the facade of the nearest first floor (or higher) noise sensitive uses, and in accordance with the latest British Standard 4142 (or any successor to this). An alternative position for assessment / measurement may be used to allow ease of access; however, this must first be agreed in writing by the local planning authority and illustrated on a map with noise propagation calculations detailed to show how the design criteria is achieved. The plant shall be isolated on adequate proprietary anti-vibration mounts to prevent the structural transmission of vibration and regenerated noise within adjacent or adjoining premises, and these shall be so maintained thereafter.
(b) Following installation of the air source heat pumps, a post completion noise assessment shall be submitted for approval to the local planning authority which demonstrates the actual measured rating level of plant operating under normal conditions. All measurements shall be made in accordance with the methodology of BS4142: 2014 (Methods for rating and assessing industrial and commercial sound) and/or its subsequent amendments. The post completion report shall be both completed and submitted to the local authority within 28 days of completion of the installation for review. If the plant fails to meet the specified standard, remedial measures shall be put in place immediately and the noise assessment shall be carried out again. This shall be repeated until the assessment has reached the required standard. 
Once achieved, the equipment shall be maintained permanently thereafter to continue to meet the standard.
Condition : 18 - The development shall be constructed to achieve the recommended internal noise levels as specified in Table 5.1 of British Standard BS8233:2014.
Prior to the first occupation of the development hereby permitted post-completion noise tests shall be carried out by accredited/approved organisations in order to demonstrate that this has been achieved. The test reports shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the local planning authority.
Noise tests shall be carried out taking account of worst-case environmental conditions, such as easterly operations at Heathrow, peak time traffic flows wind speed, direction and presence of temperature inversion. Continuous logged data shall be submitted, together with parameters measuring LAeq, 16 hours during day-time (07:00 � 23:00) and Bedroom = 30 dB LAeq, 8 hours during night-time (23:00 � 07:00), LA90 for day and night and LAFmax at 1m from external fa�ade. LAFmax 45dB inside bedrooms is applicable by default, even though this metric has been excluded from BS8233:2014; and design limit specified in BS8233:2014 for external amenity areas is also equally applicable and shall be tested for compliance.
Reason: In the interests of residential amenity.
Condition : 19 - The local planning authority shall be notified immediately if any land contamination not previously identified is encountered during development. A competent person shall assess the contamination, where necessary, including soil and groundwater sampling and testing before any further part of the development that may be affected by the additional contamination that has been discovered continues. 
A remediation method statement, prepared by a suitably qualified, experienced or supervised person, shall be submitted in writing to the local planning authority for approval within one month of the discovery of such contamination. 
Reason: Contamination is known or suspected on the site due to a former land use. It is therefore necessary to ensure that the development can be implemented and occupied with adequate regard for public and environmental safety.
Supporting notes:
(i)          Further remediation work to remove or manage additional contamination shall be carried out in accordance with the approved remediation method statement for verification and validation before the development is first brought into use. 
(ii)         In some instances, the local planning authority may require work on site to be ceased whilst the nature of additional contamination is investigated fully.
(iii)        The Council requests that the remediation method statement or any site photos be sent electronically to landquality@hounslow.gov.uk as well as being submitted to the local planning authority for approval.
Condition : 20 - The agreed scheme for remediation outlined in any approved remediation method statement, including any amendments, shall be fully implemented as part of the development. A verification report produced upon completion of the remediation by a suitably qualified, experienced or supervised person shall be submitted in writing to the local planning authority for approval, before the development is first brought into use or in accordance with a programme approved in writing by the local planning authority. 
Reason: Contamination is known or suspected on the site due to a former land use. It is therefore necessary to ensure that the development can be implemented and occupied with adequate regard for public and environmental safety.
Supporting notes:
(i)          The verification (closure) report shall revisit the conceptual site model and provide evidence that each aspect of the remediation plan has been implemented correctly and successfully in accordance with current UK guidance and best practice. Where applicable, the report shall describe how any additional/unexpected contamination encountered during development has been managed in line with the revised remediation method statement. 
(ii)         This report shall demonstrate that the development is suitable for its proposed use in terms of land quality.
(iii)        The Council requests that the verification report or site photos be sent electronically to landquality@hounslow.gov.uk as well as being submitted to the local planning authority for approval.
Condition : 21 - Prior to the commencement of development, (excluding demolition and site clearance), details of the final design of a surface water drainage scheme shall have been submitted to and approved in writing by the planning authority. The final solution should follow the principles set out in the approved drainage strategy by The EGY Collective Limited and dated 22/05/2026. The design must satisfy the SuDS Hierarchy and be compliant with the National Standards for SuDS, NPPF and Ministerial Statement on SuDS. The required drainage details shall include:
a. The results of infiltration testing completed in accordance with BRE Digest 365 and confirmation of groundwater levels. Where infiltration is proposed confirmation is required of a 1m unsaturated zone from the base of any proposed soakaway to the seasonal high groundwater level and confirmation of half-drain times.
b. Hydraulic calculations to demonstrate the prop osed final solution will effectively manage the 1 in 30 (+35% allowance for climate change) 1 in 100 (+40% allowance for climate change) storm events. If infiltration is deemed unfeasible, associated discharge rates and storage volumes shall be provided using a maximum discharge rate of 0.5 l/s.
c. Detailed design drawings for all sustainable drainage elements including cross sections and detailed drainage layout plan.
d. An exceedance flow routing plan demonstrating no increase in surface water flood risk on or off site. The plan must include proposed levels and flow directions.
e. Details of drainage management responsibilities and maintenance regimes for all drainage elements.
f. Details of how surface water will be managed during construction including measures to protect on site and downstream systems prior to the final drainage system being operational. Including details of how existing watercourse on and adjacent to the site will be protected.
The development shall be carried out in accordance with the agreed details and retained and maintained th
Condition : 22 - No demolition or development shall take place until a written scheme of investigation (WSI) has been submitted to and approved by the local planning authority in writing. For land that is included within the WSI, no demolition or development shall take place other than in accordance with the agreed WSI, which shall include the statement of significance and research objectives, and:
A.	The programme and methodology of site investigation and recording and the nomination of a competent person(s) or organisation to undertake the agreed works;
B.	Where appropriate, details of a programme for delivering related positive public benefits;
C.	The programme for post-investigation assessment and subsequent analysis, publication & dissemination and deposition of resulting material. This part of the condition shall not be discharged until these elements have been fulfilled in accordance with the programme set out in the WSI.
Reason: In order to protect the historic archaeological interest of the site. 
Supporting notes:
The written scheme of investigation will need to be prepared and implemented by a suitably professionally accredited archaeological practice in accordance with Historic England's Guidelines for Archaeological Projects in Greater London. This condition is exempt from deemed discharge under schedule 6 of The Town and Country Planning (Development Management Procedure) (England) Order 2015.
I envisage that the archaeological fieldwork would comprise a watching brief, which involves observation of groundworks and investigation of features of archaeological interest which are revealed. A suitable working method with contingency arrangements for significant discoveries will need to be agreed. The outcome will be a report and archive.
Condition : 23 - No demolition shall take place until a written scheme of historic building investigation (WSHBI) has been submitted to and approved by the local planning authority in writing. For buildings that are included within the WSHBI, no demolition or development shall take place other than in accordance with the agreed WSI, which shall include the statement of significance and research objectives, and:
A.	The programme and methodology of historic building investigation and recording and the nomination of a competent person(s) or organisation to undertake the agreed works;
B.	The programme for post-investigation assessment and subsequent analysis, publication & dissemination and deposition of resulting material. This part of the condition shall not be discharged until these elements have been fulfilled in accordance with the programme set out in the WSI.
Reason: In order to protect the historic archaeological interest of the site. 
Supporting notes:
The written scheme of investigation will need to be prepared and implemented by a suitably professionally accredited heritage practice in accordance with Historic England's Guidelines for Archaeological Projects in Greater London.
I envisage that the archaeological fieldwork would comprise a Level 3 Historic Building Recording, which is an investigation to establish the character, history, dating, form and development of a historic building or structure which normally takes place as a condition of planning permission before any alteration or demolition takes place. The outcome will be an archive and a report which may be published.
Condition : 24 - All Non-road Mobile Machinery (NRMM) used during the course of the development that is within the scope of the GLA 'Control of Dust and Emissions during Construction and Demolition' Supplementary Planning Guidance (SPG) dated July 2014, or any successor document, shall comply with the emissions requirements therein. 
The developer shall keep an up-to-date list of all NRMM used during the demolition, site preparation and construction phases of the development on the online register at https://nrmm.london/. 
Reason: In the interests of preventing harmful air quality impacts.
Condition : 25 - No development (except any demolition, site clearance, ground investigation and remediation work) shall take place until a finalised and detailed Construction Environmental Management Plan (CEMP) has been submitted to and approved in writing by the local planning authority. The CEMP shall provide details of how demolition and construction works are to be undertaken and include:
-	An identification of stages of works (including site preparation and construction stages); 
-	Procedures for maintaining good public relations including complaint management (logbook for complaints), public consultation and liaison, all in compliance with British Standards BS 5228-1:2009+A1:2014 and best practicable means;
-	Mitigation measured as defined in BS 5228: Parts 1 and 2: 2009 Noise and Vibration Control on Construction and Open Sites shall be used to minimise noise disturbance from construction works (including noise mitigation measures for all plant and processors);
-	Measures to control emissions (including dust suppression and the need to contain stored or accumulated material so as to prevent it becoming airborne at any time) during the construction phase, in line with the requirements of the Mayor's Control of Dust and Emissions during Construction and Demolition SPG, including the methods to be used and the measures to be undertaken to monitor and control the emission of dust, noise and vibration arising from construction works;
-	Details showing how all vehicles associated with the construction works are properly washed and cleaned to prevent the passage to mud and dirt onto the adjoining highway);
-	Details of provisions for recycling of materials, the provision on site of a storage/delivery area for all plant, site huts, site facilities and materials;
-	Details of a community liaison contact for the duration of all works associated with the development;
-	Any asbestos survey to be carried out; and
-	Any mobile crusher to be used on site (if required), including 
Condition : 26 - No demolition or construction work shall take place on the site except between the hours of 8:00am to 6:00pm on Mondays to Friday and 8:00am to 1:00pm on Saturdays and none shall take place on Sundays and Public Holidays without the prior agreement of the local planning authority. Additionally, HGV deliveries to the site during the course of construction will be restricted to between 9:30am and 3:00pm on Mondays to Fridays, and between 9:30am and 1:00pm on Saturdays, and none shall take place on Sundays and Public Holidays without the prior agreement of the local planning authority.
Reason: To ensure that the proposed development does not prejudice the amenities of the locality and to prevent obstruction and inconvenience to users of the public highway.
Condition : 27 - No development shall take place, (except any demolition, site clearance, ground investigation and remediation work) until a Construction Logistics Plan (CLP) that conforms to current TfL and CLOCS guidance has been submitted to, and approved in writing by, the local planning authority. The approved Plan shall be adhered to throughout the construction period. The Plan shall include: 
i.	a site plan (showing the areas set out below);
ii.	confirmation that a pre-start record of site conditions on the adjoining public highway will be undertaken with Hounslow Highways and a commitment to repair any damage to the adjoining public highway which has been caused directly by the development hereby permitted (including demolition and construction phases); 
iii.	provision for the parking of vehicles of site operatives and visitors, and any interim car parking measures that might be necessary during the construction period;
iv.	provisions for loading, unloading and storage of plant and materials within the site;
v.	details of access to the site, including means to control and manage access and egress of vehicles to and from the site for the duration of construction including phasing arrangements;
vi.	details of vehicle routeing from the site to the wider strategic road network (including hours of access, access and egress arrangements within the site and security procedures);
vii.	the erection and maintenance of security hoarding including decorative displays and facilities for public viewing, where appropriate, and clear contact details of the site manager;
viii.	provision of wheel washing facilities at the site exit and a commitment to sweep adjacent roads when required and at the request of the Council;
ix.	a scheme for recycling/disposing of waste resulting from demolition and construction works;
x.	measures to ensure the safety of all users of the public highway especially cyclists and pedestrians in the vicinity of the site and especially at the access;
xi.	comm
Condition : 28 - Before the development hereby permitted is first occupied or brought into use, a Delivery and Servicing Plan (including details of vehicle access and egress arrangements and times that servicing shall take place) shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the local planning authority. The details shall accord with current guidance such as that issued by TfL and include measures required to ensure sufficient arrangements (physical as well as managerial) for the servicing, including refuse collection, of all aspects of the development, the timing of hours for deliveries by motor vehicles and a timetable for implementation. The development shall not be carried out otherwise than in accordance with the approved details and shall be maintained for the lifetime of the development, unless the prior written approval of the local planning authority is obtained to any variation.
Reason: In the interests of the safety of pedestrians and vehicles, to protect neighbours' living conditions and to support sustainable transport objectives.
Condition : 29 - Prior to occupation a Parking Management Plan shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the local planning authority. The Plan shall include the following:
i.	details of parking allocations, including the single visitor space, and how these will be operated and enforced;
ii.	details of the EV charging provision with manufacturer's specifications;
iii.        details of how Blue Badge parking would be limited to Blue Badge holders only. 
The car parking areas shall thereafter be managed in compliance with the approved Parking Management Plan.
Reason: In order to promote sustainable modes of transport and safeguard the amenities of surrounding residential properties and ensure minimal disruption of traffic in the locality.
Condition : 30 - Secure covered cycle parking facilities (minimum 10 spaces) for the occupants of, and visitors to, the development shall be installed in the locations specified on Drawing 250119 - 1103 (Rev.P04). The approved facilities shall conform with current London Plan Cycle Parking Guidance (or such other guidance as shall supersede it) in design and layout and be fully implemented and made available for use before the first occupation of the development or commencement of the approved use as appropriate. The provisions shall thereafter be retained for use at all times without obstruction. 
Reason: To support sustainable transport objectives. 
Condition : 31 - Prior to occupation of the development, an application shall have been made to the Council's Traffic Management Order (TMO) team providing details of the TMO changes and covering any associated costs. Development shall be carried out in accordance with the agreed TMO changes, with all changes implemented prior to occupation. 
Reason: To ensure that the site access is not blocked by informal parking.
Supporting notes:
The applicant is advised to contact the Council's TMO team at: trafficorders@hounslow.gov.uk. For avoidance of doubt, previous plans to relocate a bus stop are not supported and do not form part of this planning approval. 
Condition : 32 - Prior to occupation of the development, full details of any give-way markings, including their dimensions and allowing for sufficient waiting space in front of the marking, shall have been submitted to the local planning authority and approved in writing. Development shall then be implemented in accordance with the approved details, with the markings installed and demarcated before occupation, with visibility splays for drivers and pedestrians kept clear and unobstructed at all times.
Reason: To support highway safety and unobstructed access to the site.
Condition : 33 - The development hereby permitted shall not be occupied until full details of the arrangements for the storing and management of waste and recycled materials have been submitted to and approved in writing by the local planning authority. The details shall include a refuse management strategy to ensure bins are placed in a suitable location for collection and returned to the store immediately after collection.
The arrangements for storing waste and recycled materials shall not be carried out otherwise than in accordance with any approval given and shall be completed before any part of the accommodation hereby permitted is occupied and maintained as such at all times thereafter.
Reason: In order to ensure adequate provision for waste and recycling and safeguard the amenities of the area.
description: Erection of a single storey rear extension following the demolition of the existing extension, alterations to the external facades of the building and internal alterations and reconfiguration of the property to facilitate its conversion into a children's home (Use Class C2) with associated works including installation of solar photovoltaic panels, plant and air source heat pump equipment, an access ramp with steps, landscaping, boundary treatment changes, car and cycle parking and refuse storage.
